title: Package Managers and Monorepos
summary: Install project libraries consistently and manage related packages in one repository.

subtopics.title: Dependencies
subtopics.explanation: A dependency is a library or tool that a project uses. A package manager downloads it and resolves the other packages it depends on. Put packages needed by the shipped app in `dependencies`, and build/test tools in `devDependencies`, so deployments can install the right set.

subtopics.title: Manifest and scripts
subtopics.explanation: `package.json` records project metadata, dependency ranges, and common commands. Scripts such as `build`, `lint`, and `test` give teammates and CI the same entry points. Review changes to this file because adding a package can affect bundle size, security, and install time.

subtopics.title: Lockfile
subtopics.explanation: A lockfile records the exact resolved versions and package sources for an install. Commit it so developers and CI reproduce the same dependency tree. Update it through the package manager rather than editing version entries by hand, then review the resulting changes.

subtopics.title: Workspaces
subtopics.explanation: A workspace lets one package-manager install coordinate multiple related packages in one repository. Packages can depend on one another locally, so a shared library change can be tested before publishing. Each package should still declare its own direct dependencies and build requirements.

subtopics.title: Monorepo tradeoffs
subtopics.explanation: A monorepo keeps multiple projects in one repository. Shared code and coordinated releases can become easier, but builds, permissions, and ownership need clear boundaries. Choose it when teams benefit from working together; it does not remove the need to version and test packages carefully.

foundations.overview: A package manager installs the libraries a project needs. A monorepo keeps several related packages or applications in one repository. Together, workspaces can let those projects share dependencies and test changes locally.
foundations.formalDefinition: Package managers resolve, install, and record software dependencies. A monorepo is a source repository containing multiple related projects.
foundations.whyItMatters: Consistent installs reduce “works on my machine” problems. Workspaces help teams coordinate shared packages without publishing every change first.
foundations.mentalModel: A lockfile is a recipe card with exact ingredients; a workspace is a shared workshop for several products.
foundations.browserPerspective: The package manager runs during setup and CI; its selected dependencies feed the build tool.
foundations.realWorldUsage: Use a lockfile for repeatable installs and workspaces for genuinely related packages.
foundations.businessImpact: Consistent dependency trees lower release risk and onboarding friction.
foundations.engineeringImpact: Keep package ownership and allowed dependency directions documented.
foundations.performanceImpact: Cache installs and builds carefully, then rebuild when lockfiles change.
commonUseCases: Sharing a design system across apps

commonMisconceptions.myth: A monorepo is one giant application
commonMisconceptions.reality: It can contain independently built and deployed projects.

commonMisconceptions.myth: The lockfile should not be committed
commonMisconceptions.reality: Committing it helps reproduce installs across developer machines and CI.

keyTakeaways: A dependency is a library your project uses.
A lockfile records exact package versions and their sources.
